Read an area of interest

Source: R/aoi.R
read_aoi.Rd

Reads an area of interest (AOI) from polygons, a file or bounds, and returns it as one area: an sf data frame with one row, the polygons dissolved into one polygon or multipolygon, without attributes, and optionally reprojected. It is the one entry point for AOIs in constechr, so every tool reads an AOI the same way before rasterizing or extracting data for it. To read features with their attributes, such as polygons to summarise data by, use read_layer() (and sf::st_transform() to reproject them) instead.

Usage

read_aoi(x, crs = NULL)

Arguments

x

The AOI, one of:

  • an sf data frame or sfc geometry column of polygons or multipolygons, with one feature or several. A geometry collection that holds only polygons or multipolygons is accepted too;

  • a terra SpatVector of polygons;

  • a file path (a single string) to a vector file that GDAL can read, such as a shapefile (.shp), GeoPackage (.gpkg) or GeoJSON (.geojson), read with read_layer(). To read a layer other than the first, such as one layer of a file geodatabase, name it as <path>/<layer>, for example "data.gdb/aoi". Without a layer, the first layer is read, with a message naming it if there are others;

  • bounds: a numeric vector c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) (named, in any order, or unnamed in that order), an sf bbox (from sf::st_bbox()) or a terra SpatExtent. For the bounds of a raster or any other spatial object, with its CRS, pass sf::st_bbox(r). A SpatRaster itself is not accepted, because it is ambiguous as an AOI (its extent or its cells).

crs

The target coordinate reference system (CRS): anything sf::st_crs() accepts, such as an EPSG code (3347), a WKT or "EPSG:<code>" string, a crs object, or a spatial object (sf, SpatRaster, SpatVector) whose CRS to use. NULL (the default) keeps the input's CRS. For bounds that carry no CRS (a numeric vector or a SpatExtent), crs is required and is the CRS the bounds are in.

Value

An sf data frame with one row: one POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON geometry in the target CRS (the input's when crs is NULL), in a geometry column named geometry, and no attribute columns. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Reading: files are read with read_layer() (sf::st_read(), GDAL), from the layer named in the path, or from the first layer.

  • Bounds: become one rectangle with its corners at the bounds (sf::st_as_sfc() of an sf::st_bbox()).

  • Geometry: Z and M coordinates are dropped (sf::st_zm()), so the AOI is two-dimensional. A geometry collection that holds only polygons becomes one multipolygon of them (sf::st_collection_extract(), "POLYGON"); one that holds points or lines is an error, as is a mix of polygons with points or lines, so nothing is dropped silently.

  • CRS: when crs differs from the input's CRS, the AOI is reprojected with sf::st_transform() (PROJ), which moves each vertex; edges are not densified, so a rectangle keeps its four corners. When crs is NULL or the same as the input's, coordinates are left untouched.

  • Validity: geometries are checked, not repaired, in the target CRS just before the dissolve, with sf::st_is_valid() (GEOS in a projected CRS; s2 in a geographic CRS when sf::sf_use_s2() is TRUE). Invalid geometries, such as self-intersecting polygons, are an error naming the features and why they are invalid. Repair them first, for example with sf::st_make_valid(), knowing that a repair can change their shape.

  • Dissolve: always, with sf::st_union(), after reprojection, in the target CRS, so the AOI is one area whatever the number of input features; attributes are dropped and empty geometries disappear. In a projected CRS the union is planar (GEOS). In a geographic (longitude and latitude) CRS it is spherical (s2) when sf::sf_use_s2() is TRUE, sf's default, and planar otherwise.

  • No areas or lengths are computed.

See also

read_layer() to read a vector layer's features and attributes as stored.

Other aoi: rasterize_aoi()

Examples

# From a file: the example AOI, a GeoPackage with one layer
path <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
aoi <- read_aoi(path)
aoi
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...

# Naming the layer, and reprojecting to longitude and latitude
read_aoi(file.path(path, "aoi"), crs = 4326)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -83.44661 ymin: 44.69229 xmax: -83.41441 ymax: 44.71665
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((-83.44661 44.6960...

# In the CRS of a template raster
template <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
)
read_aoi(path, crs = template)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...

# From bounds, which need a CRS
read_aoi(
  c(xmin = 1003000, ymin = 604000, xmax = 1006000, ymax = 607000),
  crs = template
)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...

# The bounds of a raster (or any spatial object), with its CRS
read_aoi(sf::st_bbox(template))
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1e+06 ymin: 6e+05 xmax: 1010000 ymax: 610000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1e+06 6e+05, 1010...
